summary: Preinstall hook fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated 727KB payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style obfuscated (underscore-hex identifiers, string-array indirection with rotation and a decoder function) and at npm install time downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, unzips it to a tmpdir, chmods it executable, and execFileSyncs it against a sibling math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB single-line file with heavy string-array/shuffle obfuscation (rotator, string/int table, decoder) marked as a Bun-compiled bundle. It is not referenced by dist/index.js (the declared library main) and has no relationship to the package's advertised 'Utilities for handling AJAX requests' purpose. Fetching an alternate language runtime specifically to execute a bundled opaque payload during preinstall bypasses Node-based install scanners. The tarball's homepage/repository point to ServiceTitan's uikit while the payload is unrelated to that project, indicating either a compromised publisher account or a squat of the scoped name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
